newsitem.title: USA: Maine library tracks celebrity reading.
newsitem.headline: Maine library tracks celebrity reading.

text.p: The Bible and the French novel "The Little Prince" are among books recommended by celebrities in an annual list compiled by a Maine librarian.

Glenna Nowell, who oversees the library in this small Maine town, released her annual "Who Reads What" list Monday. The list promotes reading by keeping track of what the stars are pulling off the book shelf.
Actor Douglas Fairbanks Jr. recommends the collected works of Dickens, Shakespeare and Kipling. Television host Barbara Walters suggests Antoine de Saint-Exupery's "The Little Prince."

Singer Clint Black told Nowell he reads the Bible, while fellow country star Reba McEntire recommended Nicholas Evans' best-seller "The Horse Whisperer." New Age performer John Tesh suggested "Look Homeward, Angel" by Thomas Wolfe.
Some celebrities have apparently taken a liking to their own words. Actress Cheryl Ladd and former Olympian Bruce Jenner listed books they had written themselves.
Not everyone is specific in their recommendations. Television game show star Vanna White said she was reading autobiographies in 1997.
Nowell began asking celebrities and world political figures what their favourite books were 10 years ago. The list is distributed to promote National Library Week, which begins on April 13.
